summary:
Bilecik province stands under the national framework applicable across Turkiye, and the sources carried for this record contain no Bilecik-specific law, enforcement practice or local ordinance. Whatever local variation exists is undocumented here, so the national picture is what a visitor to Bilecik should expect to encounter.

The most consequential pending measure is the leaked '11th Judicial Package', a draft omnibus justice package reported by Human Rights Watch on 29 October 2025. If adopted as drafted it would amend the penal and civil codes to criminalise behaviour deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality', and would punish participation in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony with up to four years in prison. The draft carried in the inventory makes no provision specific to Bilecik, so its reach would be uniform.

The same draft would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming health care, including surgery, from 18 to 25 and require permanent infertility as a precondition, while imposing penalties on health professionals who provide such care. Human Rights Watch described the package as one of the most alarming rollbacks of LGBT rights in decades. Fifteen Turkish LGBT organisations and the Turkish Medical Association oppose it.

Kaos GL's 2025 report, presented by lawyer Kerem Dikmen at its launch, finds that hostility toward LGBTI+ people has become explicit state policy rather than residual prejudice, with senior officials' hate speech and instructions issued to public institutions under a 'Year of the Family' banner creating a climate that encourages human-rights violations. Regulatory and supervisory bodies are documented as systematically restricting freedom of expression and artistic freedom.

At street level, foreign visitors are required to carry original photo identification at transit checkpoints, with fines of up to 3,000 Turkish lira for non-compliance, and police stop-and-check practice has been applied to trans people in public spaces even where the pending draft has not been enacted. Any such interaction places passport data alongside physical presentation, which is the principal outing risk facing a trans visitor in Bilecik or elsewhere in Turkiye.
tangentialFactors:
The pending draft package is a turbulence factor in itself: its contents are known from a leak rather than promulgated law, and enforcement practice has been observed running ahead of legislation, with police carrying out documentation stops against trans women during 2025 while the measure remained unpassed.

Kaos GL's characterisation of 2025 as a 'Year of the Family' situates the national climate within an official campaign framing, which is useful for comparison against other jurisdictions where hostility is informal rather than administratively directed. The restriction of expression and artistic freedom by regulatory bodies extends the effect beyond policing into public cultural life.

The opposition of fifteen LGBT organisations and the Turkish Medical Association to the draft indicates organised domestic resistance and a professional constituency willing to contest the measures, which distinguishes the situation from jurisdictions where such drafts proceed unopposed.
localsOnly:
Residents face a substantially tighter transition-care regime under the draft package: an age floor of 25 rather than 18 for gender-affirming care including surgery, a permanent infertility condition, and criminal exposure for the health professionals who provide the treatment. Whether these provisions have been enacted by the time of consultation is unresolved in the sources.

Kaos GL's report documents institutional hostility directed at residents through instructions to public bodies and through regulatory and supervisory action against expression and artistic freedom, meaning the restrictions are administered through ordinary bureaucracy rather than applied only at the point of arrest.

The 2025 findings were presented at a public launch by lawyer Kerem Dikmen, which indicates that domestic legal advocacy and public reporting on these measures continue to operate.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the '11th Judicial Package' has been enacted, amended or withdrawn since the October 2025 leak is not resolved in the sources carried here; it is described only as a draft under consideration and opposition.

No source in the inventory addresses Bilecik directly. There is no documented record of local police practice, municipal ordinances, hospital availability or incident history for this province, so the absence of a Bilecik-specific regime is an absence of sourcing rather than a finding that none exists.

The interaction between the draft's age and infertility conditions and existing regulations on gender-affirming care is not specified; whether the draft would supersede, supplement or conflict with current Health Ministry requirements is unresolved here.
